158	script_vm_destroy(script_vm_t *vm);

162	 *  resume the same global state.  Hot-reloading allows teachers to iterate on

167	script_vm_hot_reload(script_vm_t *vm);

183	 *  Call a global function that lives in the script environment.
184	 *
185	 *  Parameters:

188	 *      args          – array of arguments, may be NULL if argc == 0.
189	 *      argc          – number of arguments in args.
190	 *      rets          – pre-allocated array that receives return values.
191	 *      max_rets      – capacity of rets array.
192	 *      out_retc      – actual number of return values written (may be NULL).
193	 */
194	script_err_t
195	script_vm_call(script_vm_t   *vm,
196	               const char    *func_name,
197	               const script_val_t *args,
198	               int            argc,

200	               int            max_rets,

205	/* Register a native C function under the given global name */
206	script_err_t
207	script_vm_register_func(script_vm_t   *vm,
208	                        const char    *name,
209	                        script_cfunc_t cfunc,
210	                        void          *userdata);
211	
212	/* Register a constant (number / string) in the global table */
213	script_err_t
214	script_vm_register_const(script_vm_t *vm,
215	                         const char  *name,
216	                         script_val_t value);
217	
218	/* ----- Cross-Language Event Handling ------------------------------------- */
219	
220	/*
221	 *  Push an engine event into the VM.  The dispatcher converts the event
222	 *  payload into Lua tables, then calls any handlers that have subscribed
223	 *  through Script.subscribe(event_name, callback).  The function returns
224	 *  immediately—the VM will handle the event on the next tick.
225	 */
226	script_err_t
227	script_vm_publish_event(script_vm_t       *vm,
228	                        const struct q4q_event *evt);
229

231	 *  Dispatch all queued events.  This is invoked by the game loop once per

283	 * Set the logging callback used by the scripting subsystem.

17	
18	# QuestScript™ Scripting API
19	
20	QuestScript (file‐extension `.qsc`) is a lightweight, sandboxed
21	JavaScript-ish language embedded in C via [`qs_vm.h`](../src/qs_vm.h).
22	Its tight coupling with the event-driven ECS lets you:
23	
24	* inject level-specific logic (`on_spawn`, `on_collision`, timers, …)  
25	* prototype new physics without recompiling  
26	* build adaptive assessment flows (hints, scoring, voice-over)  
27	
28	If you are looking for *engine* or *ECS* C-level internals, see
29	`docs/ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md`.  
30	For the *resource pipeline* (images, audio, GLSL), see
31	`docs/RESOURCE_PACKS.md`.
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 📌 Quick Start
36	
37	1. Create a file `levels/lesson_02_refraction.qsc`
38	2. Add an entry point:
39	
40	```javascript
41	/// lesson_02_refraction.qsc
42	function on_level_start() {
43	    // Steer camera and drop a welcome message
44	    scene.camera.setPosition(0, 12, 18);
45	    ui.toast("Welcome to Refraction Lab!", 3.0);
46	}
47	
48	function on_laser_enter_prism(hitInfo) {
49	    // Slow-mo + sparkle when first photon hits the glass
50	    if (!state.firstHit) {
51	        physics.setTimescale(0.4);
52	        fx.sparkle(hitInfo.point, 0.8);
53	        audio.playOnce("sfx/chime.ogg");
54	        state.firstHit = true;
55	    }
56	}
57	```
58	
59	3. Bind functions to engine events in the level JSON:
60	
61	```jsonc
62	// levels/lesson_02_refraction.json
63	{
64	  // …
65	  "scripts": {
66	    "file": "lesson_02_refraction.qsc",
67	    "bindings": {
68	      "level:start"      : "on_level_start",
69	      "entity:laser:hit" : "on_laser_enter_prism"
70	    }
71	  }
72	}
73	```
74	
75	4. Press <F5>. Hot-reload will compile and attach the new script
76	   instantly—no restart required.
77	
78	---
79	
80	## Table of Contents
81	
82	- [Language Basics](#language-basics)
83	- [Runtime Lifecycle Hooks](#runtime-lifecycle-hooks)
84	- [Event Objects](#event-objects)
85	- [ECS Utilities](#ecs-utilities)
86	- [Physics API](#physics-api)
87	- [UI & Audio Helpers](#ui--audio-helpers)
88	- [Coroutines & Timers](#coroutines--timers)
89	- [Global State](#global-state)
90	- [Foreign Function Interface](#foreign-function-interface)
91	- [Debugging & Error Handling](#debugging--error-handling)
92	- [Security Sandbox](#security-sandbox)
93	- [Versioning & Compatibility](#versioning--compatibility)
94	- [Changelog](#changelog)
95	
96	---
97	
98	## Language Basics
99	
100	QuestScript syntax resembles ES5 JavaScript with the following
101	limitations (for determinism & VM size):
102	
103	* **No `eval` or `Function` constructor**  
104	* **JSON-only literals** — no `Date`, no `RegExp`  
105	* **No prototype mutation** — `Object.prototype` is frozen  
106	* `let` / `const` preferred; `var` allowed but discouraged  
107	* Tail-call recursion is *not* optimized (stack limit ~256 calls)  
108	* Garbage-collection is mark-and-sweep, triggered each frame or when
109	  memory crosses 64 KiB
110	
111	👉 For a language primer see `docs/QUESTSCRIPT_GRAMMAR.md`.
112	
113	---
114	
115	## Runtime Lifecycle Hooks
116	
117	Hook name | Signature              | When called
118	----------|------------------------|---------------------------------------------
119	`on_level_start` | `()` | After all entities/components are instantiated
120	`on_level_end`   | `(reason:string)` | Immediately before unloading the level
121	`on_spawn`       | `(entity:EID)` | Whenever an entity prefab enters the scene
122	`on_destroy`     | `(entity:EID)` | Right before an entity is recycled
123	`on_tick`        | `(dt:float)`  | Every frame *after* physics update
124	`on_pause_toggle`| `(paused:bool)` | Whenever pause state changes
125	
126	Example:
127	
128	```javascript
129	function on_tick(dt) {
130	    // rotate a spotlight at 20°/s
131	    let light = scene.entity("guiding_light");
132	    if (light) {
133	        let rot = light.getRotation();
134	        rot.y += degToRad(20) * dt;
135	        light.setRotation(rot);
136	    }
137	}
138	```
139	
140	---
141	
142	## Event Objects
143	
144	Events delivered to scripts are frozen plain objects with predictable
145	shape (all keys documented). Common event families:
146	
147	### 1. Collision Events
148	
149	Event key        | Type          | Description
150	-----------------|---------------|------------
151	`type`           | `"collision"` | Event discriminator
152	`self`           | `EID`         | The entity that owns the collider
153	`other`          | `EID`         | Entity collided with
154	`point`          | `Vec3`        | World coordinates
155	`normal`         | `Vec3`        | Collision normal (unit)
156	`impulse`        | `float`       | Magnitude (N·s)
157	
158	```javascript
159	function on_collision(e) {
160	    if (entities.tagged(e.other, "goal")) {
161	        ui.toast("Level Complete!");
162	        game.completeLevel();
163	    }
164	}
165	```
166	
167	### 2. Input Events
168	
169	Key | Value
170	----|------
171	`type` | `"key"` or `"mouse"` or `"touch"`
172	`key`  | `"W"`, `"Space"`, `"LeftClick"`, …
173	
174	Use with `input.bind("W", "onThrust")` in script.
175	
176	Full schemas live in `docs/EVENT_SCHEMAS.yaml`.
177	
178	---
179	
180	## ECS Utilities
181	
182	All entity/component manipulations route through the thin wrapper
183	`scene.*` which forwards to the C ECS.
184	
185	```javascript
186	// Spawn a photon with wavelength = 550nm
187	let eid = scene.spawn("PhotonPrefab", {
188	    wavelength: 550e-9,
189	    velocity  : vec3(0, 0, -1).scale(50)
190	});
191	```
192	
193	Available helpers:
194	
195	Category | Methods
196	---------|------------------------------------------------------
197	`scene`  | `spawn(pfb, overrides)`, `entity(name|EID)`, `destroy(e)`
198	`entities`| `withTag(tag)`, `tagged(e, tag)`, `exists(e)`
199	`components`| `get(e, "Mass")`, `set(e, "Velocity", v3)`, `has(e,"Gravity")`
200	
201	Component types exposed are auto-generated—lookup tables are generated
202	from `ecs_schema.json` at build time.
203	
204	---
205	
206	## Physics API
207	
208	Namespace `physics.*`
209	
210	Method | Arguments | Description
211	-------|-----------|------------
212	`setTimescale` | `factor:float` | Slow-down or speed-up global simulation
213	`raycast` | `origin:Vec3`, `dir:Vec3`, `dist:float` | Returns `HitInfo?`
214	`addForce` | `e:EID`, `force:Vec3`, `mode:"impulse"|"force"` | Apply to entity
215	`refract` | `incident:Vec3`, `normal:Vec3`, `n1:float`, `n2:float` | Returns new dir
216	
217	Example: Snell’s Law visualized
218	
219	```javascript
220	function predictRefraction(incidence, n1, n2) {
221	    let dir = physics.refract(incidence, vec3(0,1,0), n1, n2);
222	    gizmos.arrow(vec3(0), incidence, 1.0, 0xff0000); // red in
223	    gizmos.arrow(vec3(0), dir,       1.0, 0x00ff00); // green out
224	}
225	```
226	
227	---
228	
229	## UI & Audio Helpers
230	
231	Namespace | Samples
232	----------|-------------------------------------------------
233	`ui.*`    | `toast(text,dur)`, `dialog(title,msg)`, `progress(id,val)`
234	`audio.*` | `play(name,loop=false)`, `stop(name)`, `playOnce(sfx)`
235	
236	---
237	
238	## Coroutines & Timers
239	
240	QuestScript ships with small async helpers.
241	
242	```javascript
243	async function blink(entity, times) {
244	    for (let i=0; i<times; ++i) {
245	        entity.visible = !entity.visible;
246	        await wait(0.3);        // yields control
247	    }
248	}
249	```
250	
251	Built-ins:
252	
253	* `wait(seconds)`  
254	* `every(seconds, callback)` — returns `TimerID`  
255	* `clearTimer(id)`
256	
257	---
258	
259	## Global State
260	
261	`state` singleton is persisted across hot-reloads **within** a level
262	(but not when changing levels). Use it for:
263	
264	```javascript
265	if (!state.score) state.score = 0;
266	state.score += 10;
267	```
268	
269	Avoid storing entity IDs—they may be recycled.
270	
271	---
272	
273	## Foreign Function Interface
274	
275	Advanced users can declare C functions for high-performance sections.
276	
277	C side (`qs_bridge.c`):
278	
279	```c
280	#include "qs_vm.h"
281	static int l_noise(qs_State *L)
282	{
283	    float x = qs_toFloat(L, 1);
284	    float y = qs_toFloat(L, 2);
285	    qs_pushFloat(L, stb_perlin_noise3(x, y, 0.0f, 0, 0, 0));
286	    return 1;
287	}
288	void qs_register_engine_api(qs_State *L)
289	{
290	    qs_register(L, "noise2D", l_noise);
291	}
292	```
293	
294	Script side:
295	
296	```javascript
297	let v = noise2D(x * 0.1, y * 0.1);
298	heightMap.set(x,y, v);
299	```
300	
301	The VM enforces:
302	
303	* **No direct memory pointers**  
304	* **Value marshalling** — only numbers, strings, booleans, arrays,
305	  objects; blobs over 64 KiB are rejected.
306	
307	---
308	
309	## Debugging & Error Handling
310	
311	`F7` toggles the in-game console.
312	
313	### Try / Catch
314	
315	```javascript
316	try {
317	    riskyCall();
318	} catch (e) {
319	    log.error("Script blew up: " + e.message);
320	}
321	```
322	
323	Unhandled exceptions pause the VM and print a stack-trace including
324	source line numbers.
325	
326	### Inspector
327	
328	Press `F9` to open the live entity inspector—select a script context to
329	set breakpoints or watch variables.
330	
331	---
332	
333	## Security Sandbox
334	
335	QuestScript is restricted—no file system, no network, no OS access.
336	Escaping the sandbox terminates the script and flags the level as
337	tampered during assessments.
338	
339	---
340	
341	## Versioning & Compatibility
342	
343	Scripting VM follows semantic versioning (`major.minor.patch`).
344	
345	Engine | Script Min | Script Max | Notes
346	-------|------------|-----------|------
347	1.7.x  | 0.9.0      | 0.9.y     | Current stable
348	1.6.x  | 0.8.2      | 0.8.y     | Legacy LTS
349	
350	Use feature detection:
351	
352	```javascript
353	if (vm.version >= "0.9.10") {
354	    audio.setPitch("bgm", 0.8);
355	}
356	```
357	
358	---
359	
360	## Changelog
361	
362	### 2.3.0 → (2024-06-04)
363	
364	* Added `physics.refract` helper
365	* Coroutine `every()` now returns handle
366	* Event schema docs moved to YAML
367	
368	### 2.2.1 → (2024-04-11)
369	
370	* Object pool recycle callback `on_destroy` exposed
371	* `ui.progress` supports color parameter
372	
373	---
374	
375	## Appendices
376	
377	### A. Built-in Math Constants
378	
379	Name | Value
380	-----|------
381	`TAU`| 6.283185307179586
382	`PHI`| 1.61803398875
383	`SPEED_OF_LIGHT`| 299792458.0
384	
385	### B. Standard Library Size Metrics
386	
387	| Category  | SLOC | Footprint (KiB) |
388	|-----------|------|-----------------|
389	| VM Core   | 3 102| 79              |
390	| Bindings  |   645| 18              |
391	| Std Lib   |   988| 24              |
392	
393	---
394	
395	Happy tinkering, and may your photons always find the optimal path! 💡
396	```

2	# Quest for Quantum – System Architecture
3	
4	> Version: 1.2  
5	> Updated: 2023-10-15  
6	> Maintainer: core@questforquantum.dev
7	
8	Quest for Quantum (Q4Q) is a medium-scale, event-driven 2-D/2.5-D game simulation written in portable C11.  
9	This document is a high-level but _implementation-oriented_ tour of the architecture.  
10	It is meant for developers contributing to the engine or creating advanced educational scenarios.
11	
12	---
13	
14	## Table of Contents
15	1. Architectural Viewpoints
16	2. Directory & Module Layout
17	3. Runtime Component Map  
18	   3.1 Game Loop & Phases  
19	   3.2 Event Bus & Command Pattern  
20	   3.3 Entity-Component-System (ECS) Core  
21	   3.4 Scripting & Hot-Reload  
22	   3.5 Object Pool for Particles  
23	   3.6 Resource Manager  
24	   3.7 Audio, UI & Tooling
25	4. Subsystem Interaction Diagram
26	5. Memory, Concurrency & Error Handling
27	6. Data-Driven Workflow
28	7. Build & Deployment
29	8. Contributing Guidelines
30	
31	---
32	
33	## 1. Architectural Viewpoints
34	
35	| View            | Rationale                                                                                 |
36	|-----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
37	| Logical         | Clarify responsibilities of subsystems (ECS, scripting, I/O).                             |
38	| Process/Thread  | Explain minimal parallelism (audio mixing, background loading).                          |
39	| Deployment      | Show target platforms (Desktop, WebAssembly + AudioWorklet).                             |
40	| Development     | Provide ground rules for adding features without breaking determinism or STEM fidelity.   |
41	
42	---
43	
44	## 2. Directory & Module Layout
45	
46	```
47	QuestForQuantum
48	 ├─ src
49	 │   ├─ core            # Engine essentials (event bus, memory, time)
50	 │   ├─ ecs             # Entity/Component/System implementation
51	 │   ├─ systems         # Physics, optics, audio, AI
52	 │   ├─ io              # Window, input, platform abstractions
53	 │   ├─ script          # byte-code VM & bindings
54	 │   ├─ editor          # Level editor & debugging UI
55	 │   └─ assets          # Embedded asset manifest (auto-gen)
56	 ├─ data
57	 │   ├─ levels          # JSON/TOML scenario definitions
58	 │   └─ shaders         # GLSL/HLSL
59	 ├─ docs
60	 │   └─ ARCHITECTURE.md # <— this file
61	 ├─ tests               # Unit & property tests (μTest + fuzz)
62	 └─ build               # CMake & CI scripts
63	```
64	
65	The code base sits at ~140 k tokens (≈ 64k LOC including headers).
66	
67	---
68	
69	## 3. Runtime Component Map
70	
71	### 3.1 Game Loop & Phases
72	
73	The engine runs a classical *fixed-time-step, variable-render* loop tuned to 60 Hz physics and ≤ 240 Hz rendering.  
74	High-level pseudocode:
75	
76	```c
77	while (!core_should_quit()) {
78	    core_poll_events();         // Non-blocking input & OS messages
79	    core_accumulate_time();     // fixedDelta ≈ 16.667 ms
80	    while (core_step_pending()) {
81	        event_bus_flush();      // Dispatch queued events
82	        ecs_run_systems();      // Physics, AI, scripts (deterministic)
83	        script_vm_tick();       // Interpret 1 byte-code slice
84	    }
85	    renderer_draw();            // Interpolate transforms, swap buffers
86	    audio_mixer_submit();       // Low-latency, on separate thread
87	}
88	```
89	
90	Determinism is preserved inside the fixed-delta block; anything after `renderer_draw()`
91	may be frame-skipped.
92	
93	---
94	
95	### 3.2 Event Bus & Command Pattern
96	
97	Every stimulus—keypress, collision, or timeline cue—becomes a heap-
98	allocated `Q4Q_Event` pushed into a lock-free SPSC queue (`core/event_bus.c`).
99	
100	```c
101	typedef enum {
102	    EVT_KEY_DOWN, EVT_SPAWN_PHOTON, EVT_COLLISION, /* … */
103	} Q4Q_EventType;
104	
105	typedef struct {
106	    Q4Q_EventType   type;
107	    Q4Q_TimeStamp   ts;
108	    union {                     // Event-specific payload
109	        struct { int key; }              key;
110	        struct { uint32_t proto_id; }    spawn;
111	        struct { ent_id a, b; }          collision;
112	    };
113	} Q4Q_Event;
114	```
115	
116	The Command Pattern appears when systems *subscribe* to event families via a tiny DSL:
117	
118	```c
119	EVENT_SUBSCRIBE(collision_system, EVT_COLLISION, handle_collision);
120	EVENT_SUBSCRIBE(optics_system,    EVT_SPAWN_PHOTON, spawn_photon);
121	```
122	
123	`event_bus_flush()` iterates over queued events once per physics tick, guaranteeing in-order delivery and constant time removal.
124	
125	### 3.3 Entity-Component-System Core
126	
127	• **Entity**: 32-bit handle (`ent_id`), recycled via generational free list.  
128	• **Component**: Plain structs (POD) stored in SoA arrays, e.g.:
129	
130	```c
131	typedef struct { vec2 pos, vel; float mass; } cmp_rigidbody;
132	typedef struct { float wavelength_nm; float phase; } cmp_photon;
133	```
134	
135	• **System**: Stateles functions iterating over *archetype views*:
136	
137	```c
138	static void gravity_system(float dt, q4q_view v) {
139	    cmp_transform* t; cmp_rigidbody* rb;
140	    VIEW_ITER(v, t, rb) { rb->vel.y += 9.81f * dt; }
141	}
142	```
143	
144	Component storage is **hot-swappable** via `cmp_registry`, allowing
145	teachers to add new attribute sets without touching core code.
146	
147	### 3.4 Scripting & Hot-Reload
148	
149	We embed a bespoke stack-based VM (`script/q4q_vm.*`) with:
150	
151	* Byte-code compiled from a Lua-like syntax  
152	* Deterministic integer math & `double` for science accuracy  
153	* Host API auto-generated from headers via `clang-python`
154	
155	Scripts can be recompiled at runtime:
156	
157	```
158	:reload optics_refraction.q4q
159	```
160	
161	The engine detects file hashes and spawns a *background compiler thread*; the new
162	byte-code replaces the old one atomically at VM tick boundaries.
163	
164	### 3.5 Object Pool for Particles
165	
166	Photon entities can number in the thousands.  
167	`pool/photon_pool.c` pre-allocates N=4096 entries, each 128 bytes, fitting inside L2.
168	
169	Key points:
170	
171	* Free list embedded in unused photons → O(1) spawn/kill  
172	* Generation counters prevent stale `ent_id` reuse  
173	* Periodic maintenance recycles “decayed” photons by half-life
174	
175	### 3.6 Resource Manager
176	
177	`res_cache.*` handles:
178	
179	* Texture, shader, audio clip, and VM byte-code streams  
180	* Memory-mapped files when supported (POSIX, Win32)  
181	* Reference counting + weak handles for ECS components
182	
183	On hot-reload, the cache retains immutable *handles*; systems see a
184	new `void*` pointer transparently after the loading thread finishes.
185	
186	### 3.7 Audio, UI & Tooling
187	
188	* **Audio**: real-time parametric synthesis (square, sine, noise); frequency = photon wavelength → ear-training  
189	* **UI**: `dear-c-imgui` style immediate mode; rendered on top of SDL or GLFW backend  
190	* **Level Editor**: shipped as an in-game overlay; serializes to `data/levels/<name>.json`
191	
192	---
193	
194	## 4. Subsystem Interaction Diagram
195	
196	```mermaid
197	flowchart LR
198	    Input -->|events| EventBus
199	    Timeline -->|events| EventBus
200	    Physics --> ECS
201	    Optics --> ECS
202	    EventBus --> ECS
203	    ECS --> ScriptVM
204	    ScriptVM --> ECS
205	    ECS --> Renderer
206	    ECS --> Audio
207	    Renderer --> Window
208	    Audio --> AudioDevice
209	    ResourceCache --> Renderer
210	    ResourceCache --> ScriptVM
211	```
212	
213	---
214	
215	## 5. Memory, Concurrency & Error Handling
216	
217	### Memory Model
218	
219	* Arena allocator for level → frees at unload  
220	* Frame arena (`core/frame_alloc.c`) resets every render frame  
221	* Object pools for high-churn entities  
222	* `Q4Q_ASSERT()` active in debug; `core_log_error()` in release  
223	* 64-bit pointers; optional 32-bit builds via `Q4Q_PTR_SIZE=4`
224	
225	### Threading
226	
227	```
228	Thread 0 (Main)   : Game loop, ECS, renderer submission
229	Thread 1 (Worker) : Background IO + hash compile
230	Thread 2 (Audio)  : Low-latency mixing (double-buffered ring)
231	```
232	
233	Locking strategies:
234	
235	* SPSC queues (events, compile jobs)  
236	* Read-mostly data races avoided using `atomic_uint` generation counters  
237	* Renderer uses double-buffered command lists
238	
239	### Error Handling
240	
241	* Fatal -> graceful fallback (`core_panic()`) with backtrace and JSON dump  
242	* Recoverable -> propagate via `Q4Q_Result` enum (`Q4Q_OK / ERR_*`)  
243	* `core_errstr(errno)` converts OS error codes
244	
245	---
246	
247	## 6. Data-Driven Workflow
248	
249	Example `level001.json`:
250	
251	```json
252	{
253	  "title": "Snell's Sandbox",
254	  "entities": [
255	    { "prototype": "photon", "pos": [0, 3], "wavelength": 620 },
256	    { "prototype": "glass_block", "pos": [5, 1], "n": 1.5 }
257	  ],
258	  "scripts": ["refraction_intro.q4q"],
259	  "goals": [
260	    { "type": "hit_target", "id": "sensor_exit" }
261	  ]
262	}
263	```
264	
265	Teachers edit JSON, reload, and the engine produces an event
266	`EVT_LEVEL_RELOAD`. No C recompilation required.
267	
268	---
269	
270	## 7. Build & Deployment
271	
272	* **CMake ≥ 3.20** generates projects for GCC/Clang/MSVC & Emscripten  
273	* `-std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror`  
274	* `SANITIZE=address,undefined` in CI (GitHub Actions)  
275	* Artifact size: Desktop ≈ 4 MiB stripped; WebAssembly ≈ 2.7 MiB gzipped  
276	* Portable save files: MessagePack with `crc32` integrity
277	
278	---
279	
280	## 8. Contributing Guidelines
281	
282	1. All public APIs live in `include/q4q/*.h`; no malloc in headers.  
283	2. Run `make format` (clang-format) before PR.  
284	3. Add **unit tests** in `tests/` and fuzz harness if input parsing.  
285	4. Keep physics deterministic; avoid `rand()` inside fixed-update.  
286	5. Document new events in `docs/EVENTS.md`.  
287	6. Prefer data-oriented design; no virtual function tables.  
288	7. Feature flags go behind `#ifdef Q4Q_EXPERIMENTAL_<NAME>`.
289	
290	---
291	
292	_Quest for Quantum_ turns a middle-school lesson into an experiential playground.  
293	This architecture balances **scientific accuracy**, **performance**, and **modability**—ready for your next pull request!
294	
295	---
296	```

2	# Quest for Quantum – Level File Format Specification
3	Version: **1.4**  
4	Status: **Stable / Production**  
5	Last Updated: 2024-03-09  
6	Applies to Engine: `QuestForQuantum >= 0.9.0`  
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 1. Overview
11	Quest for Quantum levels are defined in a **strict-subset** of JSON called **QON (Quantum Object Notation)**.  
12	Files are UTF-8 encoded and carry the extension `.qon`. The engine streams and parses the
13	content through the in-house `qon_reader.c`, so round-tripping between editor and runtime is lossless.
14	
15	Design Goals  
16	• Human-readable & git-friendly (no binary blobs).  
17	• Forward-compatible through semver **`"format": "major.minor"`** field.  
18	• Supports hot-reloading and partial updates over TCP in the classroom multi-screen mode.  
19	
20	---
21	
22	## 2. Top-Level Schema
23	```jsonc
24	{
25	  "format": "1.4",
26	  "metadata": {...},
27	  "settings": {...},
28	  "entities": [ ... ],
29	  "scripts": [ ... ],
30	  "timeline": [ ... ],
31	  "$comment": "QON allows // and /* */ comments when loaded by the engine."
32	}
33	```
34	
35	| Field      | Type      | Required | Description                                                |
36	|------------|-----------|----------|------------------------------------------------------------|
37	| format     | string    | yes      | Semantic version of the level file format.                 |
38	| metadata   | object    | yes      | Human-facing information such as title, author, etc.       |
39	| settings   | object    | yes      | Physics/environment knobs – gravity, refractive index …    |
40	| entities   | array     | yes      | ECS entities with component collections.                   |
41	| scripts    | array     | no       | Inline script modules (Lua subset) bound to events.        |
42	| timeline   | array     | no       | Key-frame events evaluated by the **Timeline System**.     |
43	
44	---
45	
46	## 3. Metadata Block
47	```jsonc
48	"metadata": {
49	  "title": "Snell’s Window",
50	  "author": "J. Doe, 8th Grade",
51	  "description": "Explore refraction angles between water and air surfaces.",
52	  "created": "2024-02-14T09:43:00Z",
53	  "revision": 3,
54	  "tags": ["refraction", "optics", "puzzle"]
55	}
56	```
57	
58	---
59	
60	## 4. Settings Block
61	```jsonc
62	"settings": {
63	  "gravity": [0.0, -9.81],      // X,Y components; units m/s²
64	  "ambient_light": 0.25,        // 0.0 – 1.0
65	  "audio_theme": "underwater",
66	  "refractive_index": {
67	    "medium_a": 1.000293,       // Air
68	    "medium_b": 1.333           // Water
69	  },
70	  "bounds": {                   // Playfield rectangle in metres
71	    "x": -15, "y": 0, "w": 30, "h": 20
72	  }
73	}
74	```
75	
76	---
77	
78	## 5. Entity Specification
79	
80	### 5.1 Structure
81	```jsonc
82	{
83	  "id": "photon-player-01",
84	  "prefab": "avatars/photon",
85	  "components": {
86	    "Transform":   { "position": [0, 2], "rotation": 0 },
87	    "Physics":     { "mass": 0.0, "velocity": [1.0, 0.0] },
88	    "Photon":      { "wavelength_nm": 550, "polarization": "linear" },
89	    "Input":       { "maps": ["default"] },
90	    "Collider":    { "shape": "circle", "radius": 0.25, "layer": 3 }
91	  },
92	  "onSpawn": "init_player"
93	}
94	```
95	
96	### 5.2 Reserved Component Names
97	• `Transform` – mandatory for spatial entities  
98	• `Physics`    – integrates with the **Physics System**  
99	• `Collider`   – registers with **Collision System**  
100	• `Renderable` – draws sprite/mesh; supports animation sets  
101	• `AudioSource`– attaches positional audio emitter  
102	
103	### 5.3 Prefabs
104	If **`prefab`** is present, the engine loads a template from
105	`assets/prefabs/<path>.qon`. Component values declared in the entity override prefab defaults (deep-merge).
106	
107	---
108	
109	## 6. Script Modules
110	Each entry in `"scripts"` is an object:
111	
112	```jsonc
113	{
114	  "id": "init_player",
115	  "language": "lua",               // Engine currently supports "lua" only.
116	  "source": "function(e) e:emit('PLAYER_INITIALIZED') end"
117	}
118	```
119	
120	The engine injects the following API into the script sandbox:
121	
122	| Function            | Purpose                                       |
123	|---------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
124	| `e:get(comp)`       | Fetch component table (read-only).            |
125	| `e:set(comp, tbl)`  | Merge values into component.                  |
126	| `e:emit(evt, data)` | Broadcast custom event on the Event Bus.      |
127	| `delay(sec, fn)`    | Schedule callback in Timeline System.         |
128	
129	---
130	
131	## 7. Timeline Events
132	Useful for cut-scenes or phased challenges.
133	
134	```jsonc
135	"timeline": [
136	  { "t": 0.00, "event": "PLAY_MUSIC",   "args": { "track": "intro" } },
137	  { "t": 4.50, "event": "SHOW_TEXT",    "args": { "key": "welcome" } },
138	  { "t": 8.00, "event": "ENABLE_INPUT", "args": {} }
139	]
140	```
141	
142	Engine guarantees **±1 ms** accuracy in the fixed update loop.
143	
144	---
145	
146	## 8. Asset References
147	Paths are *virtual* and resolved by the **Resource Manager** using search
148	directories declared in `engine.cfg`. Example:
149	
150	```
151	avatars/photon        -> assets/prefabs/avatars/photon.qon
152	music/underwater      -> assets/audio/music/underwater.ogg
153	```
154	
155	---
156	
157	## 9. Minimal Example Level
158	```jsonc
159	{
160	  "format": "1.4",
161	  "metadata": { "title": "Hello Refraction", "author": "QfQ Team" },
162	  "settings": { "gravity": [0, -9.81], "ambient_light": 0.3 },
163	  "entities": [
164	    {
165	      "id": "photon-player-01",
166	      "prefab": "avatars/photon",
167	      "components": {
168	        "Transform": { "position": [-5, 3] },
169	        "Input": {}
170	      }
171	    },
172	    {
173	      "id": "water-surface-01",
174	      "components": {
175	        "Transform": { "position": [0, 0] },
176	        "Collider": { "shape": "line", "length": 30 },
177	        "RefractiveBoundary": { "n1": 1.0, "n2": 1.333 }
178	      }
179	    }
180	  ]
181	}
182	```
183	
184	---
185	
186	## 10. Loader Integration (C Snippet)
187	
188	```c
189	/*
190	 * level_loader.c – runtime integration of .qon files
191	 */
192	#include "qon_reader.h"
193	#include "ecs.h"
194	#include "systems.h"
195	#include "logging.h"
196	
197	bool level_load_from_file(const char *path)
198	{
199	    QonDoc *doc = qon_read_file(path);
200	    if (!doc) {
201	        LOG_ERROR("Failed to read level: %s", path);
202	        return false;
203	    }
204	
205	    // Validate format version
206	    const char *fmt = qon_get_string(doc, "/format");
207	    if (!fmt || strncmp(fmt, "1.", 2) != 0) {
208	        LOG_ERROR("Unsupported level format '%s' in %s", fmt ? fmt : "NULL", path);
209	        qon_destroy(doc);
210	        return false;
211	    }
212	
213	    // Load settings
214	    LevelSettings settings;
215	    if (!parse_settings(doc, &settings)) {
216	        LOG_ERROR("Invalid settings block in %s", path);
217	        qon_destroy(doc);
218	        return false;
219	    }
220	    apply_level_settings(&settings);
221	
222	    // Spawn entities
223	    QonNode *entities = qon_get_node(doc, "/entities");
224	    if (!entities || entities->type != QON_ARRAY) {
225	        LOG_ERROR("Missing entities array in %s", path);
226	        qon_destroy(doc);
227	        return false;
228	    }
229	
230	    for (size_t i = 0; i < entities->size; ++i) {
231	        if (!spawn_entity_from_qon(entities->items[i])) {
232	            LOG_WARN("Entity #%zu failed to spawn (continuing)", i);
233	        }
234	    }
235	
236	    // Register timeline events & scripts
237	    register_timeline(doc);
238	    register_scripts(doc);
239	
240	    LOG_INFO("Successfully loaded level '%s'", path);
241	    qon_destroy(doc);
242	    return true;
243	}
244	```
245	
246	---
247	
248	## 11. Best Practices and Gotchas
249	1. **IDs must be unique.** The ECS hashes `id` into a 32-bit handle; collisions cause undefined behavior.  
250	2. **Avoid floating-point drift** by resetting long-running timeline loops every 10 minutes.  
251	3. **Zero-mass entities** (photons) are not simulated by the physics solver; they rely on custom kinematics.  
252	4. When overriding prefab components, unspecified keys are untouched—clear them explicitly with `null`.  
253	
254	---
255	
256	## 12. Change Log
257	• **1.4** – Added `refractive_index.medium_*` pair, deprecated single `n`.  
258	• **1.3** – `timeline` now supports sub-millisecond precision (float).  
259	• **1.2** – Introduced `$comment` field; loader ignores unknown top-level keys.  
260	• **1.1** – Added `tags` array in `metadata`.  
261	• **1.0** – Initial release.  
262
